chunks: And from him from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father from Isma'il ibn Isa who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah) during the month of Ramadan and slept until morning; what is upon him? He said: 'This does not harm him and he does not break his fast, for my father (peace be upon him) said: 'Aishah said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became junub from intercourse, not from wet dream.' He said: 'He does not break his fast and it does not matter to him.'
And a man who incurred major ritual impurity and remained sleeping until morning; what is obligatory upon him? He said: 'Nothing is upon him; he performs ghusl.'

And a man who incurred major ritual impurity in the last part of the night and rose to perform ghusl but did not find water, so he went to seek it or sent someone to bring it, and it was difficult for him until morning; what should he do? He said: 'He performs ghusl when it comes to him, then he prays.'
And as for that which indicates the second category, it is what he narrated:

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: The last part of the night
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash
key_terms.جُنُباً: In a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping in a state of janabah break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that sleeping in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) does not invalidate the Ramadan fast, citing the precedent of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as reported by Aisha. The narration distinguishes between scenarios where water is accessible versus scarce, emphasizing that the obligation is to perform ghusl upon availability before prayer, rather than imposing immediate fasting penalties for the delay. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that janabah itself is not a cause for breaking the fast, provided one intends to purify themselves for the day's worship.
